agentCan: Implement the authorization-code flow with strict refresh-rotation discipline
Register clients at runtime via RFC 7591, or host a Client ID Metadata Document, for agent/MCP clients
Implement revocation (legacy and RFC 7009 endpoints) and 401 refresh-and-retry handling

approval.cost: Free ('You can use our API for free'; feature availability can depend on account plan)
approval.trigger: No pre-connection review is stated in the developer docs: console-registered (or dynamically registered) apps can run the OAuth flow with no documented approval step, timeline, or fee. An official integrations list exists ('submitted for evaluation and inclusion'), but its criteria and timeline live outside the developer docs. Instead of review, Todoist enforces limits: exceeding the application's maximum token limit, or abuse suspension, surfaces as an invalid_application_status error at authorize time. The limit's value is not published.

blockers.detail: Refresh tokens rotate on every successful refresh. Replay a consumed token WITHIN 60 seconds and it is treated as a network retry (you get the same replacement access token but NO refresh token in the response; you must have kept the original). Replay it AFTER the grace window and it 'is treated as a potential replay attack: all access and refresh tokens issued to the user for the application are revoked', and the user must re-authorize.
blockers.howToClear: Serialize refreshes per user, persist the newest refresh token atomically, and never retry a refresh blindly.
blockers.title: Refresh replay outside 60 seconds revokes everything

blockers.detail: For legacy apps, enabling refresh tokens in the console 'cannot be disabled' once on: all new tokens follow the refresh flow, while tokens issued before opting in remain long-lived and are not converted. Newly created apps have refresh tokens enabled by default.
blockers.howToClear: Treat the toggle as a permanent migration decision and plan token storage for both populations during transition.
blockers.title: Refresh tokens are a one-way door

blockers.detail: An 'Invalid Application Status' error at authorize time means your application exceeded its maximum token limit or was suspended for abuse. The maximum exists but its value is not stated anywhere in the docs read, so you cannot plan capacity against a published number.
blockers.howToClear: Monitor token counts, revoke dead tokens proactively, and design for graceful degradation if authorization starts failing.
blockers.title: An unstated maximum token limit can suspend your app

alternatives: Dynamic Client Registration, RFC 7591 (for clients that cannot pre-register: 'multi-tenant integrations, MCP servers, and AI agents acting on behalf of an end user'; POST /oauth/register, unauthenticated, returns a tdd_-prefixed client_id)
Client ID Metadata Documents (zero registration: client_id is an HTTPS URL to a JSON metadata document; for public clients that cannot store a secret; PKCE mandatory)
Personal API token (single user; Settings > Integrations > Developer)
flavor.recommended: An application in the App Management Console (app.todoist.com) with refresh tokens enabled, standard authorization code flow
flavor.why: The docs steer multi-user products to OAuth ('Building for other people? Use OAuth authorization instead of a personal token'). Refresh tokens are enabled by default for newly created applications. Notably, Todoist is one of the few providers with first-class registration paths designed for agents and MCP servers (see alternatives), worth using when your client cannot pre-register or hold a secret.

humanMust: Create the application in the App Management Console and configure redirect URLs
Copy and vault the Client ID and Client Secret
Follow the brand rules (name format 'x for Todoist', plus the not-affiliated disclaimer)
name: Todoist
nuances: Legacy apps without refresh tokens issue effectively permanent tokens: the docs show expires_in 315360000, 'a 10-year compatibility value rather than a meaningful expiry'. Refresh-enabled apps get 1-hour access tokens.

Scopes are few and coarse: task:add (add only), data:read, data:read_write (includes both), data:delete, project:delete, backups:read. Mind the separators: comma-separated in the authorize URL, space-separated in dynamic registration.
On refresh you may request only a narrower subset of the original grant; asking beyond it errors.

Metadata-document constraints are tight: HTTPS URL with a path beyond '/', publicly routable IP (private/loopback rejected for SSRF protection), max 5KB, 5-second fetch timeout, redirects not followed, token_endpoint_auth_method must be 'none', PKCE required.
Brand rules with teeth: 'Todoist' cannot be the primary name of your app, and your description must state it is 'not created by, affiliated with, or supported by Todoist'.
prerequisites: One or more valid OAuth2 redirect URLs
Your scope set (few and coarse: data:read / data:read_write family)

steps.detail: In the App Management Console (app.todoist.com), create the application and configure one or more valid OAuth2 redirect URLs. Refresh tokens are enabled by default for new apps (legacy apps opt in via the console, irreversibly). Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Register the application

steps.detail: Redirect the user to app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope (comma-separated), state (unique and unguessable; abort if it comes back unmatched), and redirect_uri (REQUIRED if multiple redirect URIs are configured; omitting it is rejected). Denials return error=access_denied.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST to api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token with client_id, client_secret, and code. Refresh-enabled apps receive expires_in 3600 plus a refresh_token and the granted scope.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Refresh at the same endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token. Rotation is strict: always store the latest refresh token; respect the 60-second retry semantics and never replay outside it (see Blockers). Revoke via the documented legacy or RFC 7009 revocation endpoints.
steps.title: Refresh with rotation discipline

steps.detail: If your client cannot pre-register (MCP server, multi-tenant agent): POST to api.todoist.com/oauth/register (RFC 7591; up to 10 redirect URIs, HTTPS required, restricted scopes rejected, grant_types must include authorization_code). Or host a Client ID Metadata Document and use its URL as client_id with mandatory PKCE.
steps.title: (Agent/MCP path) Register dynamically or use a metadata document

tagline: Textbook OAuth with the strictest refresh-token replay rules in this library: reuse a consumed token after a 60-second grace window and Todoist revokes every token that user has with your app. Also home to two registration flows built specifically for AI agents.

time.active: ~10 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day; no review to wait on
